Name: Strangler Fig
Strategy: Route new requests to new system while old system handles legacy traffic
Risk: Medium — partial failure during dual-running period
Rollback Plan: Revert routing rules to send all traffic back to monolith
Gotcha: Must maintain feature parity during transition; data sync between old and new is the hardest part

Name: Dual Write
Strategy: Write to both old and new data stores simultaneously during migration
Risk: High — inconsistency if one write fails; ordering issues
Rollback Plan: Stop writes to new system; reconcile from old system as source of truth
Gotcha: Dual writes are inherently unsafe without distributed transactions; prefer CDC instead

Name: Change Data Capture (CDC)
Strategy: Stream changes from source DB via transaction log to target systems
Risk: Low-Medium — CDC is eventually consistent; schema changes can break connectors
Rollback Plan: Stop CDC connector; target system uses last known good state
Gotcha: Schema evolution in source DB can silently break CDC pipelines; monitor connector lag

Name: Expand-Contract Schema
Strategy: Add new columns/tables first (expand); migrate data; remove old columns (contract)
Risk: Low — backward compatible at each step
Rollback Plan: Reverse the contract step; re-add old columns
Gotcha: Never drop old columns until all consumers have migrated; use feature flags

Name: Blue-Green Database
Strategy: Maintain two identical databases; switch traffic atomically
Risk: Medium — data divergence during sync window
Rollback Plan: Switch back to blue database; replay missed writes from green
Gotcha: Bidirectional replication is complex; prefer unidirectional with brief read-only cutover window

Name: Parallel Run
Strategy: Run old and new systems simultaneously; compare outputs; serve from old
Risk: Low — old system serves all traffic; new system is shadow
Rollback Plan: Stop parallel run; no user impact since old system is primary
Gotcha: Comparing outputs is harder than it sounds — timestamps and IDs will differ; normalize before comparing

Name: Trickle Migration
Strategy: Move data in small batches over time to avoid big-bang risk
Risk: Low per batch — but total duration increases risk of schema drift
Rollback Plan: Stop trickle; reconcile what has migrated vs what hasn't
Duration Estimate: Weeks to months depending on volume
Gotcha: Must handle records modified after migration; need reconciliation pass at the end

Name: Feature Flag Migration
Strategy: Use feature flags to gradually shift traffic from old to new implementation
Risk: Low — instant rollback by flipping flag; % rollout controls blast radius
Rollback Plan: Flip flag back to old implementation (instant)
Gotcha: Feature flag debt accumulates; schedule flag cleanup after migration completes

Name: API Version Migration
Strategy: Run old and new API versions simultaneously; deprecate old over time
Risk: Medium — maintaining two versions doubles test surface
Rollback Plan: Keep v1 running longer; communicate extended deprecation timeline
Gotcha: Set deprecation headers from day 1; monitor v1 usage to know when safe to remove

Name: Zero-Downtime Cutover
Strategy: Atomic switch from old to new with no service interruption
Risk: High — requires perfect sync; any missed writes cause data loss
Rollback Plan: Reverse DNS/routing to old system; replay from WAL/CDC
Duration Estimate: Hours for cutover event (weeks of prep)
Gotcha: Practice the cutover multiple times in staging; have a clock-based abort threshold

Name: Database Sharding Migration
Strategy: Redistribute data across new shard topology
Risk: High — resharding while serving traffic requires careful coordination
Rollback Plan: Revert shard map to old topology; replay missed writes
Gotcha: Consistent hashing with virtual nodes minimizes data movement; test with shadow traffic first

Name: Monolith Decomposition
Strategy: Extract bounded contexts from monolith into separate services
Risk: High — shared database and entangled code make extraction difficult
Rollback Plan: Keep extracted service but route traffic back to monolith code path
Gotcha: Start with the least entangled domain; extract data layer before code layer

Name: Cloud Provider Migration
Strategy: Move workloads from one cloud provider to another
Risk: Very High — different APIs and services; rewrite infrastructure code
Rollback Plan: Maintain old cloud environment until new is proven stable
Gotcha: Managed services (RDS → Cloud SQL) require the most rework; use Terraform for abstraction

Name: Queue/Broker Migration
Strategy: Migrate from one message broker to another
Risk: High — message ordering and exactly-once guarantees differ between brokers
Rollback Plan: Run old broker in parallel; consumers can switch back
Gotcha: Schema registries don't transfer; consumer group offsets need manual mapping

Name: Kubernetes Migration
Strategy: Move workloads to Kubernetes from VMs or other orchestrators
Risk: Medium-High — networking and storage models are fundamentally different
Rollback Plan: Keep old orchestrator running; shift traffic back via load balancer
Gotcha: Stateful workloads (databases) should often stay on VMs; don't migrate everything
